items.rationale: The washing-machine escape is covered under §2.4.2, and §7.1.7(h) covers cleaning the wetted floor. Allow €85 for one cleaning item, calibrated to the combined charge in Case 12.
The hallway floor was also reached by the escaped water, so §7.1.7(h) covers its cleaning. Allow €85 for one cleaning item, calibrated to Case 12.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers checking the source and confirming that it no longer leaks, even if the appliance itself is not insured. Allow €95 for one connection check.
Section 7.1.7(a) covers taking down and disposing of the damaged skirting. Allow €65 for one removal and disposal item.

Fixed skirting is a building component under §4.2.2, and §§7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 allow like-for-like replacement. Allow €145 for one installed replacement item; lines 1–5 total €475, within the Case 12 combined range.
Sections 3.5 and 7.1.5 exclude both operations because the bedroom was not reached by the water. The €550 estimate is the conditional gross price for one combined item.
Section 7.1.7(b) covers measuring moisture in the two affected rooms. Allow €165 for the single billed survey, using Case 21's €153–178 range as the closest separate measurement reference.
Section 7.1.7(b) covers necessary drying of the affected floor areas. Allow €180 for one drying item, excluding the separately priced rental and labour because §7.1.8(c) bars duplicate charges.

Section 7.1.7(e) expressly covers equipment hire for necessary drying, provided it is not already charged in line 8. Allow €145 for one rental item; lines 7–10 total €642, within the Case 12 combined range.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary trade labour, subject to the duplicate-cost exclusion in §7.1.8(c). The supplied labour prior gives 4 hours × €38 = €152 gross.
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) exclude measurement and drying in this separate, unaffected room. The €425 estimate is the conditional gross price for one combined item.

Section 5.2.6 makes specialist transport eligible but gives restoration first call on the shared €1,190 gross cap. Restoration is expected to exhaust that cap; if a balance remains, transport is next in invoice order, up to an estimated €110 gross.
Section 5.2.6 covers specialist assessment only from the balance after restoration and the earlier transport line. No balance is expected; €135 is the conditional estimate if sufficient cap remains.

items.description: Drying and stabilisation of hallway painting
items.rationale: Section 5.2.6 covers stabilisation but allocates the cap first to restoration, then to transport and assessment in invoice order. No balance is expected; €180 is the conditional estimate if sufficient cap remains.

Full specialist restoration of the affected, ornately framed painting is expected to exceed the unscheduled-item limit in §5.2.6, which applies first to restoration. With incurred VAT recoverable under §7.7 for this private household, €1,000 × 1.19 = €1,190 gross.

Section 5.2.6 requires the item itself to have been affected by the insured event, which this painting was not. The €1,190 estimate is the conditional gross ceiling for a qualifying unscheduled painting, not an allowance for this line.

Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes separately billed administration and processing charges, and §5.2.6 does not list them as conservation costs. The €35 figure is a conditional estimate for one flat fee, not an allowance.
